items.q: How do I buy a CS2 skin in Uzbekistan?
items.a: Sign in with Steam, add your trade link and pick a skin in the market. Pay with Click, Payme, Uzum or from your balance — the skin arrives in Steam as a trade offer.

items.q: How do I pay for skins in soʻm?
items.a: With Click, Payme or Uzum — using a Uzcard or Humo card. You can also top up the site balance and buy from it. No foreign card needed.
The money goes back to your site balance by itself. You can spend it on another skin.

items.q: Why can’t I trade a bought skin right away?
items.a: That is Steam’s trade protection: for 7 days the item sits in your inventory but cannot be traded or sold. The rule is the same on every marketplace. After a week the skin is fully yours.

items.q: Where do I find my Steam trade link?
items.a: Steam → Inventory → Trade offers → “Who can send me trade offers?”. Copy the link and paste it in your csmarket profile.

items.q: How do I sell CS2 skins for soʻm?
items.a: Open “Sell skins”, pick items from your inventory and send the trade. The money goes to your site balance or to a Uzcard, Humo or Uzum Visa card.

items.q: Do you need my Steam password?
items.a: No. Sign-in is only through Steam’s official page. We never ask for your password or Steam Guard codes.

about.title: A CS2 skins shop in Uzbekistan
about.intro: csmarket.uz is a Counter-Strike 2 skins market made for players in Uzbekistan: prices in soʻm, local payment methods and a site in Russian and Uzbek.

blocks.h: How to buy CS2 skins in Uzbekistan
blocks.p: The csmarket catalogue holds thousands of items: knives, gloves, rifles, pistols, SMGs, cases, agents, charms and keys. Prices are in soʻm, so there is no need to convert dollars or watch the exchange rate. Pick a skin, pay the way you like — and the item arrives in Steam as a trade offer. To buy, sign in with Steam and add your trade link: the site shows where to find it.

blocks.h: Pay in soʻm: Click, Payme, Uzum
blocks.p: Pay with what you use every day: Click, Payme or Uzum, with a Uzcard or Humo card. You don’t need a foreign card, Visa or Mastercard. You can top up the site balance and buy from it — handy when you take several skins in a row. If a trade fails for any reason, the money returns to your balance by itself, ready for another skin.

blocks.h: How the skin arrives in Steam
blocks.p: After payment you receive a trade offer in Steam. Open it in the Steam app or in a browser, check the item and confirm. The order status is shown in your account. We never ask for your login, password or Steam Guard codes — you sign in only through Steam’s official page, and your account stays yours.

Steam protects trades for 7 days. During that time the skin is already in your inventory and you can play with it, but you cannot trade or sell it. It is a Steam rule, it applies on every marketplace and protects buyers from scams. After a week the restriction lifts and the item is fully yours.

Knives and gloves are the most visible items in the game. They are marked with a star (★), drop very rarely from cases and hold their value well. The market has Karambit, Butterfly Knife, M9 Bayonet, Bayonet, Talon, Skeleton, and gloves such as Sport Gloves, Specialist Gloves, Driver Gloves, Hand Wraps and more. Doppler and Gamma Doppler knives come in phases (Phase 1–4, Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald) — the phase is shown right on the skin card.

The glow colour of a card shows its rarity: from Consumer Grade and Mil-Spec to Classified, Covert and Contraband. Wear changes the look and the price: Factory New, Minimal Wear, Field-Tested, Well-Worn and Battle-Scarred. StatTrak™ means a kill counter on the weapon, Souvenir a tournament souvenir version. Filters by price, wear, rarity and StatTrak™ find the skin you want in a couple of clicks — from cheap skins to rare knives.

You can sell us the skins you no longer need. Sign in with Steam, pick items from your inventory and send the trade. The money goes to your site balance or to a Uzcard, Humo or Uzum Visa card — whichever suits you. Spend the balance on new skins right away: upgrade your knife, build a one-colour inventory or get gloves for your favourite weapon.

blocks.h: The site in Russian, Uzbek and English
blocks.p: The site works in three languages: Russian, Uzbek and English. csmarket is for everyone who wants to buy CS2 skins in Tashkent, Samarkand, Bukhara, Namangan, Andijan, Fergana or any other city of Uzbekistan.
